subject: Plain-language console blurb and subprocessor commitments
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acme.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick: short console blurb + subprocessor commitments

Hi Soojin —

We’re finalizing our procurement packet and need a concise, customer-facing sentence (or two) about how Redwood handles subprocessors and cross-border transfers for the hosted API that we can drop into our privacy appendix and the console UI. A couple of specific questions:

- Do you rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or another transfer mechanism for EU transfers?
- Will we get a subprocessor list snapshot that we can publish/attach?
- What is the notice period when Redwood adds a new subprocessor?

If you can give us a short blurb and a few FAQ bullets we’ll include it with our DPA review. Thanks — we need something customer-ready by end of day.

Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: short console blurb + subprocessor commitments

Hi Tom —

Thanks for the quick ask. Below is a customer-facing blurb plus a short FAQ we propose for the console and your procurement appendix. I’ve attached a snapshot of our current subprocessor roster and a doc with the blurb in two length options.

Proposed console blurb (short):
"Redwood Inference uses vetted subprocessors to operate the hosted API. Data is transferred under contractually binding safeguards; customers may request the current subprocessor list and we provide advance notice before material changes."

FAQ bullets (short):
- Transfer mechanism: We use EU-approved transfer safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses) and additional technical controls where required.
- Subprocessor list: Attached — we provide a downloadable snapshot on request and publish a summary in the console.
- Notice for changes: We provide at least 30 days’ notice for planned additions to the subprocessor roster; for urgent operational/critical security changes we will notify customers as soon as reasonably practical.
- DPA: Our DPA and privacy policy reference these commitments; we can provide a copy to procurement.

Attachments: console_priv_blurb_v1.docx (two length options + usage notes), subprocessor_list_snapshot.csv (current as of 2026-11-29). Also putting a link to the Drive doc here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1qZ-drive-docs-console-blurb

Would you like the blurb shortened further for the compact console card, or is the short sentence above okay? Kimberly and Laura are looped to confirm legal language.

Best,
So—
So, Soojin Lee
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Thanks, Soojin — tagging in legal clearance. A few edits and clarifications we should make before publishing that text in the console or a procurement packet:

1) Transfer mechanism: say "EU-approved transfer safeguards (e.g., Standard Contractual Clauses)" rather than implying SCCs are the sole mechanism. That leaves room for equivalent safeguards.

2) Avoid absolute claims like "we provide advance notice" without qualification. Suggest: "we provide advance notice for planned changes (typically 30 days) and will notify customers as soon as reasonably practicable for urgent operational changes."

3) Encryption/controls language: if we reference technical safeguards, use "industry-standard encryption in transit and at rest" rather than specifics unless we include a link to the security FAQ.

4) Subprocessor snapshot: add a short usage line: "A downloadable snapshot is available on request; customers can also subscribe to console notifications for roster updates."

With those edits, legal signs off. Laura — can you confirm the attachment matches the snapshot we publish in the console and update the file name to include the date (e.g., subprocessor_list_20261129.csv)?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
